title: Disrupting supply chain attacks on npm and GitHub Actions
excerpt: Explore the changes we've shipped across npm and GitHub Actions over the past few months to disrupt supply chain attack techniques and limit their impact.
content_html:
Explore the changes we’ve shipped across npm and GitHub Actions over the past few months to disrupt supply chain attack techniques and limit their impact.

July 28, 2026

|

7 minutes

  • Share:

In the past year, there’s been a pattern of supply chain attacks that target weaknesses in package repositories and CI/CD systems to quickly spread malware to hundreds of open source projects. This malware seeks to exfiltrate credentials both to broadly spread the attack, as well as for later exploitation.

We’ve written a few times about our plans for hardening the supply chain: Our plan for a more secure npm supply chain in September 2025, Strengthening supply chain security: Preparing for the next malware campaign in December 2025, and What’s coming to our GitHub Actions 2026 security roadmap in March 2026. In this post, we’re updating you on changes we’ve implemented that directly disrupt some of the most common and impactful supply chain attack techniques.

Anatomy of supply chain attacks

Supply chain attacks chain together several weaknesses, and there is no single security capability that can stop them. Addressing them takes a holistic approach, prioritizing the mitigations that break the most impactful links in the attack chain. Our teams have been studying these attacks to deploy several improvements that disrupt them and limit their impact. This is possible thanks to collaboration with the security research and developer communities.

The attacks vary in how they spread across the software ecosystem. However, most of these attacks follow similar techniques to gain initial access to a project, escalate privileges, and distribute across users and software. Improvements made to npm and GitHub Actions in the past few months have been focused on cutting off specific, common techniques and providing ways for customers to identify and respond to these attacks.

Initial compromise

Attacks start by compromising a single project, often by directly compromising a maintainer’s account or by targeting the project’s actions workflows.

  • npm adds preventive account protection for high-impact accounts (June 2026): Frequently, attacks start with a phishing campaign targeting maintainers. With this change, high-impact npm accounts are now put into a read-only mode for 72 hours when they change their email or use a 2FA recovery code. This delay allows maintainers time to respond and recover the account before their account can be used to start an attack.
  • Safer pull_request_target defaults for GitHub Actions checkout (June 2026): A common vulnerability in a project’s CI/CD pipelines are “pwn requests,” where a workflow triggers on pull requests from forks and then executes user-submitted and untrusted code from that fork. We changed the default behavior of actions/checkout to prevent the checkout of untrusted code from forks in commonly exploited triggers unless you explicitly opt-out (after reviewing your risk). This change and its backport to older versions cut off one of the most common vulnerable code patterns leading to code execution in GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows and initial project compromise.
  • Control who and what triggers GitHub Actions workflows (June 2026): Maybe you’d prefer to opt-out of these risky action triggers altogether or limit who can trigger them. This new control lets you set enterprise, organization, or repository level policies on who is allowed to trigger workflows and what trigger types are allowed. These workflow execution policies provide a governable and customizable layer of least-privilege around Action workflows that reduce the attack surface of your CI/CD infrastructure.
  • Read-only Actions cache for untrusted triggers (June 2026): After an attacker has achieved code execution in an Actions workflow, they then look to escalate to more privileged workflows (and therefore credentials) through poisoning the cache entries shared across workflows. With this change, we restrict the ability for less trusted workflows to modify the cache shared with other workflows. This directly closes a common path attackers have used to turn a vulnerability with limited impact into one that compromises highly privileged credentials used by release and publishing workflows.

Exfiltrate credentials

Once an attacker has access to a single package, they then focus on detecting and exfiltrating credentials to gain further access and use in later exploitation across ecosystems.

  • npm trusted publishing now supports CircleCI (April 2026): The number one thing you can do to disrupt these attacks is to remove long-lived credentials from your CI/CD pipeline. Trusted publishing is a great way to authorize publishes to your package repository without a long-lived credential. By adding CircleCI as a trusted publishing provider, we’ve made it possible for more people to remove the credentials these attacks attempt to exfiltrate.
  • Actions network firewall (In technical preview): This technical preview logs all outbound network traffic from your Action workflow runs so you can detect unusual behavior like pulling down malicious code or exfiltrating credentials to a new domain. Future work will enable network egress restrictions and policies to block these attacks before they lead to further escalation and exfiltration.

Propagating the attack

With the credentials harvested from the previous step, attackers attempt to use those credentials to distribute their malware and compromise more projects and maintainers as quickly as possible.

  • Staged publishing for npm (May 2026): With staged publishing, it’s not enough to have credentials to publish a new package on npm; those packages are staged until additional approval and 2FA authentication is provided in the npm cli or on npmjs.com. This opt-in security control allows maintainers to ensure that any version of their package published has gone through this additional authorization. By decoupling the credentials used in CI/CD pipelines and automation from those that can publish to the registry, the attack chain from a CI/CD pipeline to malware distribution is cut off.
  • Upcoming breaking changes for npm v12 (June 2026): To spread their malware as quickly as possible, attackers use npm install-time scripts to exfiltrate credentials instead of waiting for code to be executed by the package at runtime. With npm v12, we are rolling out a breaking change that disables these install scripts by default. Since install scripts have legitimate use within the package installation processes that several popular packages rely on, you can reenable them by approving specific scripts. Additional vectors for install-time code execution have also been blocked by disabling dependencies via git or remote URLs by default.
  • Dependabot version updates introduce default package cooldown (July 2026): Attackers rely on speed, hoping a malicious release gets pulled into as many downstream projects as possible before anyone notices. Version updates through Dependabot now wait until a release has been available for at least three days before opening a pull request, giving detection signals time to surface before a malicious release reaches your project. This cooldown is on by default, and security updates still open immediately, so critical fixes are never delayed.

Identifying and responding to supply chain attacks

In parallel to hardening npm and GitHub Actions to disrupt and limit the impact of supply chain attacks, we have also been working on making features and tools available to users to identify and respond to supply chain incidents that have impacted their projects and accounts.

  • Self-service credential revocation for incident response (June 2026): GitHub credentials remain an ongoing target of attackers in supply chain attacks. This feature provides self-service tooling to instantly revoke all credentials for a given user in an enterprise. This builds on the enterprise-wide credential management tools for incident response released in February and allows enterprise admins and members to quickly respond if credentials have been compromised in a supply chain attack.
  • Expanded credential revocation API support (March 2026): Recent attacks have included exfiltrating credentials within publicly accessible content. To help the community respond to these attacks, we have expanded support of our credential revocation API (first introduced in April 2025 for personal access tokens) to support the revocation of GitHub OAuth and App tokens. This allows the quick and self-service revocation of these leaked credentials, regardless of where they are found, and limits the lifetime during which they can be abused.

What’s Next?

Making our products more secure by default is a priority across npm and GitHub and we are prioritizing this work to target and disrupt supply chain attacks across the open source ecosystem. We’re proud of the work we’ve shipped towards this goal over the past months. There’s more to come, but we wanted to provide an update on the progress we’ve made and make folks aware of the new capabilities available to them. Be sure to follow our changelog and blog posts as we continue to roll out improvements.

Open source software is an incredible public good that we all benefit from, and this is one of several ways GitHub is working to continue to support the security, sustainability, and continued success of open source communities and the enterprises that depend on them.

Written by

Principal Product Security Engineer

Principal Software Engineer, GitHub

sentences.zh: npm 可信发布现在支持 CircleCI（2026 年 4 月）：要阻止这些攻击，您可以做的第一件事就是从 CI/CD 管道中删除长期有效的凭据。

sentences.en: Trusted publishing is a great way to authorize publishes to your package repository without a long-lived credential.
sentences.zh: 可信发布是一种无需长期凭据即可授权发布到包存储库的好方法。

sentences.en: By adding CircleCI as a trusted publishing provider, we’ve made it possible for more people to remove the credentials these attacks attempt to exfiltrate.
sentences.zh: 通过将 CircleCI 添加为值得信赖的发布提供商，我们使更多的人能够删除这些攻击试图窃取的凭据。

blocks.html_en: • Actions network firewall (In technical preview): This technical preview logs all outbound network traffic from your Action workflow runs so you can detect unusual behavior like pulling down malicious code or exfiltrating credentials to a new domain. Future work will enable network egress restrictions and policies to block these attacks before they lead to further escalation and exfiltration.

sentences.en: Actions network firewall (In technical preview): This technical preview logs all outbound network traffic from your Action workflow runs so you can detect unusual behavior like pulling down malicious code or exfiltrating credentials to a new domain.
sentences.zh: Actions 网络防火墙（技术预览版）：此技术预览版会记录 Action 工作流程运行中的所有出站网络流量，以便您可以检测异常行为，例如拉取恶意代码或将凭据泄露到新域。

sentences.en: Future work will enable network egress restrictions and policies to block these attacks before they lead to further escalation and exfiltration.
sentences.zh: 未来的工作将使网络出口限制和策略能够在这些攻击导致进一步升级和渗透之前阻止这些攻击。

blocks.html_en: Propagating the attack

sentences.en: Propagating the attack
sentences.zh: 传播攻击

blocks.html_en: With the credentials harvested from the previous step, attackers attempt to use those credentials to distribute their malware and compromise more projects and maintainers as quickly as possible.

sentences.en: With the credentials harvested from the previous step, attackers attempt to use those credentials to distribute their malware and compromise more projects and maintainers as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 通过上一步获取的凭据，攻击者尝试使用这些凭据来分发恶意软件并尽快危害更多项目和维护人员。

blocks.html_en: • Staged publishing for npm (May 2026): With staged publishing, it’s not enough to have credentials to publish a new package on npm; those packages are staged until additional approval and 2FA authentication is provided in the npm cli or on npmjs.com. This opt-in security control allows maintainers to ensure that any version of their package published has gone through this additional authorization. By decoupling the credentials used in CI/CD pipelines and automation from those that can publish to the registry, the attack chain from a CI/CD pipeline to malware distribution is cut off.

sentences.en: Staged publishing for npm (May 2026): With staged publishing, it’s not enough to have credentials to publish a new package on npm; those packages are staged until additional approval and 2FA authentication is provided in the npm cli or on npmjs.com.
sentences.zh: npm 的分阶段发布（2026 年 5 月）：通过分阶段发布，仅仅拥有在 npm 上发布新包的凭据是不够的；这些包将被暂存，直到 npm cli 或 npmjs.com 中提供额外批准和 2FA 身份验证。

sentences.en: This opt-in security control allows maintainers to ensure that any version of their package published has gone through this additional authorization.
sentences.zh: 这种选择加入的安全控制允许维护者确保其发布的任何版本的软件包都经过了这种额外的授权。

sentences.en: By decoupling the credentials used in CI/CD pipelines and automation from those that can publish to the registry, the attack chain from a CI/CD pipeline to malware distribution is cut off.
sentences.zh: 通过将 CI/CD 管道和自动化中使用的凭证与可以发布到注册表的凭证解耦，从 CI/CD 管道到恶意软件分发的攻击链被切断。

blocks.html_en: • Upcoming breaking changes for npm v12 (June 2026): To spread their malware as quickly as possible, attackers use npm install-time scripts to exfiltrate credentials instead of waiting for code to be executed by the package at runtime. With npm v12, we are rolling out a breaking change that disables these install scripts by default. Since install scripts have legitimate use within the package installation processes that several popular packages rely on, you can reenable them by approving specific scripts. Additional vectors for install-time code execution have also been blocked by disabling dependencies via git or remote URLs by default.

sentences.en: Upcoming breaking changes for npm v12 (June 2026): To spread their malware as quickly as possible, attackers use npm install-time scripts to exfiltrate credentials instead of waiting for code to be executed by the package at runtime.
sentences.zh: npm v12（2026 年 6 月）即将发生的重大更改：为了尽快传播恶意软件，攻击者使用 npm 安装时脚本来窃取凭据，而不是等待包在运行时执行代码。

sentences.en: With npm v12, we are rolling out a breaking change that disables these install scripts by default.
sentences.zh: 在 npm v12 中，我们推出了一项重大更改，默认情况下禁用这些安装脚本。

sentences.en: Since install scripts have legitimate use within the package installation processes that several popular packages rely on, you can reenable them by approving specific scripts.
sentences.zh: 由于安装脚本在多个流行软件包所依赖的软件包安装过程中具有合法用途，因此您可以通过批准特定脚本来重新启用它们。

sentences.en: Additional vectors for install-time code execution have also been blocked by disabling dependencies via git or remote URLs by default.
sentences.zh: 默认情况下，通过 git 或远程 URL 禁用依赖项，还可以阻止安装时代码执行的其他向量。

blocks.html_en: • Dependabot version updates introduce default package cooldown (July 2026): Attackers rely on speed, hoping a malicious release gets pulled into as many downstream projects as possible before anyone notices. Version updates through Dependabot now wait until a release has been available for at least three days before opening a pull request, giving detection signals time to surface before a malicious release reaches your project. This cooldown is on by default, and security updates still open immediately, so critical fixes are never delayed.

sentences.en: Dependabot version updates introduce default package cooldown (July 2026): Attackers rely on speed, hoping a malicious release gets pulled into as many downstream projects as possible before anyone notices.
sentences.zh: Dependabot 版本更新引入了默认包冷却时间（2026 年 7 月）：攻击者依赖速度，希望在任何人注意到之前将恶意版本引入尽可能多的下游项目。

sentences.en: Version updates through Dependabot now wait until a release has been available for at least three days before opening a pull request, giving detection signals time to surface before a malicious release reaches your project.

sentences.en: This cooldown is on by default, and security updates still open immediately, so critical fixes are never delayed.
sentences.zh: 默认情况下，此冷却时间处于开启状态，并且安全更新仍会立即打开，因此关键修复永远不会延迟。

blocks.html_en: Identifying and responding to supply chain attacks

sentences.en: Identifying and responding to supply chain attacks
sentences.zh: 识别并响应供应链攻击

blocks.html_en: In parallel to hardening npm and GitHub Actions to disrupt and limit the impact of supply chain attacks, we have also been working on making features and tools available to users to identify and respond to supply chain incidents that have impacted their projects and accounts.

sentences.en: In parallel to hardening npm and GitHub Actions to disrupt and limit the impact of supply chain attacks, we have also been working on making features and tools available to users to identify and respond to supply chain incidents that have impacted their projects and accounts.
sentences.zh: 在强化 npm 和 GitHub Actions 以破坏和限制供应链攻击影响的同时，我们还一直致力于为用户提供可用的功能和工具，以识别和响应影响其项目和帐户的供应链事件。

blocks.html_en: • Self-service credential revocation for incident response (June 2026): GitHub credentials remain an ongoing target of attackers in supply chain attacks. This feature provides self-service tooling to instantly revoke all credentials for a given user in an enterprise. This builds on the enterprise-wide credential management tools for incident response released in February and allows enterprise admins and members to quickly respond if credentials have been compromised in a supply chain attack.

sentences.en: Self-service credential revocation for incident response (June 2026): GitHub credentials remain an ongoing target of attackers in supply chain attacks.
sentences.zh: 用于事件响应的自助凭证撤销（2026 年 6 月）：GitHub 凭证仍然是供应链攻击中攻击者的持续目标。

sentences.en: This feature provides self-service tooling to instantly revoke all credentials for a given user in an enterprise.
sentences.zh: 此功能提供自助服务工具，可立即撤销企业中给定用户的所有凭据。

sentences.en: This builds on the enterprise-wide credential management tools for incident response released in February and allows enterprise admins and members to quickly respond if credentials have been compromised in a supply chain attack.
sentences.zh: 它建立在 2 月份发布的用于事件响应的企业范围凭证管理工具的基础上，如果凭证在供应链攻击中受到损害，企业管理员和成员可以快速响应。

blocks.html_en: • Expanded credential revocation API support (March 2026): Recent attacks have included exfiltrating credentials within publicly accessible content. To help the community respond to these attacks, we have expanded support of our credential revocation API (first introduced in April 2025 for personal access tokens) to support the revocation of GitHub OAuth and App tokens. This allows the quick and self-service revocation of these leaked credentials, regardless of where they are found, and limits the lifetime during which they can be abused.

sentences.en: Expanded credential revocation API support (March 2026): Recent attacks have included exfiltrating credentials within publicly accessible content.
sentences.zh: 扩展凭证撤销 API 支持（2026 年 3 月）：最近的攻击包括在可公开访问的内容中窃取凭证。

sentences.en: To help the community respond to these attacks, we have expanded support of our credential revocation API (first introduced in April 2025 for personal access tokens) to support the revocation of GitHub OAuth and App tokens.
sentences.zh: 为了帮助社区应对这些攻击，我们扩大了对凭证撤销 API（首次于 2025 年 4 月针对个人访问令牌推出）的支持，以支持撤销 GitHub OAuth 和应用程序令牌。

sentences.en: This allows the quick and self-service revocation of these leaked credentials, regardless of where they are found, and limits the lifetime during which they can be abused.
sentences.zh: 这允许快速、自助地撤销这些泄露的凭证，无论它们在哪里被发现，并限制它们被滥用的生命周期。

content_html_zh:
探索过去几个月我们在 npm 和 GitHub Actions 上发布的更改，以破坏供应链攻击技术并限制其影响。

July 28, 2026

|

7分钟

  • Share:

在过去的一年里，出现了一种针对软件包存储库和 CI/CD 系统中的弱点的供应链攻击模式，以将恶意软件快速传播到数百个开源项目。 该恶意软件旨在窃取凭据以广泛传播攻击以及供以后利用。

我们已经多次撰写了有关强化供应链的计划：我们计划在 2025 年 9 月建立更安全的 npm 供应链，加强供应链安全：为 2025 年 12 月的下一次恶意软件活动做准备，以及 2026 年 3 月我们的 GitHub Actions 2026 安全路线图将会发生什么。 在这篇文章中，我们将向您介绍我们已实施的更改，这些更改直接破坏了一些最常见和最有影响力的供应链攻击技术。

供应链攻击剖析

供应链攻击将多个弱点联系在一起，并且没有单一的安全功能可以阻止它们。 解决这些问题需要采取整体方法，优先考虑破坏攻击链中最有影响力的环节的缓解措施。 我们的团队一直在研究这些攻击，以部署多项改进措施来破坏这些攻击并限制其影响。 这要归功于与安全研究和开发者社区的合作。

这些攻击在软件生态系统中传播的方式各不相同。 然而，大多数这些攻击都遵循类似的技术来获得对项目的初始访问权限、升级权限以及跨用户和软件进行分发。 过去几个月对 npm 和 GitHub Actions 的改进主要集中在切断特定的通用技术，并为客户提供识别和响应这些攻击的方法。

初步妥协

攻击从危害单个项目开始，通常是直接危害维护者的帐户或针对项目的操作工作流程。

  • npm 为高影响力帐户添加了预防性帐户保护（2026 年 6 月）：攻击通常始于针对维护者的网络钓鱼活动。 通过此更改，高影响力的 npm 帐户现在在更改电子邮件或使用 2FA 恢复代码时将进入只读模式 72 小时。 这种延迟使维护人员有时间响应并恢复帐户，然后才能使用其帐户发起攻击。
  • GitHub Actions checkout 的默认 pull_request_target 更安全（2026 年 6 月）：项目 CI/CD 管道中的一个常见漏洞是“pwn 请求”，其中工作流触发来自分叉的拉取请求，然后从该分叉执行用户提交的不受信任的代码。 我们更改了操作/签出的默认行为，以防止从常用触发器中的分叉中签出不受信任的代码，除非您明确选择退出（在检查风险后）。 此更改及其向后移植到旧版本切断了最常见的易受攻击的代码模式之一，导致 GitHub Actions CI/CD 工作流程中的代码执行和初始项目妥协。
  • 控制触发 GitHub Actions 工作流程的人员和内容（2026 年 6 月）：也许您更愿意完全选择退出这些有风险的操作触发器或限制可以触发它们的人员。 通过此新控件，您可以设置企业、组织或存储库级别的策略，确定允许谁触发工作流以及允许哪些触发器类型。 这些工作流执行策略围绕操作工作流提供可管理且可自定义的最低权限层，从而减少 CI/CD 基础设施的攻击面。
  • 用于不受信任触发器的只读操作缓存（2026 年 6 月）：攻击者在操作工作流中实现代码执行后，他们会通过毒害跨工作流共享的缓存条目来升级到更高特权的工作流（以及凭据）。 通过此更改，我们限制了不太受信任的工作流修改与其他工作流共享的缓存的能力。 这直接关闭了攻击者将影响有限的漏洞转变为危害发布和发布工作流程使用的高特权凭据的常见路径。

窃取凭证

一旦攻击者能够访问单个包，他们就会专注于检测和窃取凭据，以便在以后跨生态系统的利用中获得进一步的访问和使用。

  • npm 可信发布现在支持 CircleCI（2026 年 4 月）：要阻止这些攻击，您可以做的第一件事就是从 CI/CD 管道中删除长期有效的凭据。 可信发布是一种无需长期凭据即可授权发布到包存储库的好方法。 通过将 CircleCI 添加为值得信赖的发布提供商，我们使更多的人能够删除这些攻击试图窃取的凭据。
  • Actions 网络防火墙（技术预览版）：此技术预览版会记录 Action 工作流程运行中的所有出站网络流量，以便您可以检测异常行为，例如拉取恶意代码或将凭据泄露到新域。 未来的工作将使网络出口限制和策略能够在这些攻击导致进一步升级和渗透之前阻止这些攻击。

传播攻击

通过上一步获取的凭据，攻击者尝试使用这些凭据来分发恶意软件并尽快危害更多项目和维护人员。

  • npm 的分阶段发布（2026 年 5 月）：通过分阶段发布，仅仅拥有在 npm 上发布新包的凭据是不够的；这些包将被暂存，直到 npm cli 或 npmjs.com 中提供额外批准和 2FA 身份验证。 这种选择加入的安全控制允许维护者确保其发布的任何版本的软件包都经过了这种额外的授权。 通过将 CI/CD 管道和自动化中使用的凭证与可以发布到注册表的凭证解耦，从 CI/CD 管道到恶意软件分发的攻击链被切断。
  • npm v12（2026 年 6 月）即将发生的重大更改：为了尽快传播恶意软件，攻击者使用 npm 安装时脚本来窃取凭据，而不是等待包在运行时执行代码。 在 npm v12 中，我们推出了一项重大更改，默认情况下禁用这些安装脚本。 由于安装脚本在多个流行软件包所依赖的软件包安装过程中具有合法用途，因此您可以通过批准特定脚本来重新启用它们。 默认情况下，通过 git 或远程 URL 禁用依赖项，还可以阻止安装时代码执行的其他向量。
  • Dependabot 版本更新引入了默认包冷却时间（2026 年 7 月）：攻击者依赖速度，希望在任何人注意到之前将恶意版本引入尽可能多的下游项目。 现在，通过 Dependabot 进行的版本更新会等到版本发布至少三天后才打开拉取请求，从而在恶意版本到达您的项目之前让检测信号有时间浮出水面。 默认情况下，此冷却时间处于开启状态，并且安全更新仍会立即打开，因此关键修复永远不会延迟。

识别并响应供应链攻击

在强化 npm 和 GitHub Actions 以破坏和限制供应链攻击影响的同时，我们还一直致力于为用户提供可用的功能和工具，以识别和响应影响其项目和帐户的供应链事件。

  • 用于事件响应的自助凭证撤销（2026 年 6 月）：GitHub 凭证仍然是供应链攻击中攻击者的持续目标。 此功能提供自助服务工具，可立即撤销企业中给定用户的所有凭据。 它建立在 2 月份发布的用于事件响应的企业范围凭证管理工具的基础上，如果凭证在供应链攻击中受到损害，企业管理员和成员可以快速响应。
  • 扩展凭证撤销 API 支持（2026 年 3 月）：最近的攻击包括在可公开访问的内容中窃取凭证。 为了帮助社区应对这些攻击，我们扩大了对凭证撤销 API（首次于 2025 年 4 月针对个人访问令牌推出）的支持，以支持撤销 GitHub OAuth 和应用程序令牌。 这允许快速、自助地撤销这些泄露的凭证，无论它们在哪里被发现，并限制它们被滥用的生命周期。

接下来是什么？

默认情况下，让我们的产品更加安全是 npm 和 GitHub 的首要任务，我们优先考虑这项工作，以针对和破坏整个开源生态系统的供应链攻击。 我们对过去几个月为实现这一目标所做的工作感到自豪。 还有更多内容即将推出，但我们希望提供我们所取得的进展的最新信息，并让人们了解他们可以使用的新功能。 当我们继续推出改进时，请务必关注我们的变更日志和博客文章。

开源软件是一项令人难以置信的公共利益，我们都从中受益，这是 GitHub 致力于继续支持开源社区和依赖它们的企业的安全性、可持续性和持续成功的多种方式之一。
